beginner.headline: Pilot Stabbed on Flight, Passengers Help Land Plane
beginner.brief: Israel's Prime Minister said it is too early to know if Iran was involved in the flight attack. A pilot stabbed another pilot on a plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The plane lost 17,000 feet quickly, but passengers and crew stopped the attacker and landed safely. The pilot who was stabbed is Captain Smit Machchhar, and he is now stable in hospital. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called Captain Machchhar a "true hero." The attacker was arrested in Saudi Arabia and will go to the UAE. Flydubai said two crew members who were traveling landed the plane safely. The attacker tried to crash the plane.

intermediate.headline: Pilot Attempts Hijacking on Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight
intermediate.brief: Israel's Prime Minister stated it is not yet clear if Iran was connected to an incident where a pilot attempted to hijack a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The Flydubai plane suddenly dropped over 5,200 meters two hours into its trip on Wednesday. Passengers and cabin staff then managed to overpower the individual causing the disturbance, preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster. The injured pilot, Captain Smit Machchhar, is recovering in hospital. A passenger, Yaniv Hayun, explained how he stopped the individual trying to disable the plane, with help from others. The person accused of the attack was arrested in Saudi Arabia and is expected to be moved to the UAE, where the flight originated. Early findings from an Israeli investigation suggest the individual intended to crash the aircraft. Two hours into the journey, the aircraft dropped significantly and then signaled an emergency, followed by a hijacking code. Flydubai confirmed that two on-duty cabin staff travelling on the flight landed the plane safely. All of the airline's flights to and from Israel will be suspended during the ongoing investigation.

advanced.headline: Pilot Hailed a Hero After Foiling Mid-Air Attack on Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight
advanced.brief: It is too early to say if Iran had any involvement in an attack by a pilot who stabbed another pilot and tried to take over a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, Israel's prime minister has said. The Flydubai plane plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two hours into its journey on Wednesday, before passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control to land safely. One passenger, Yaniv Hayun, described how he put the attacker, who was trying to disable the plane, in a chokehold before other passengers helped pin him down. The alleged attacker, who was arrested in Saudi Arabia, is expected to be transferred to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), where the plane took off from, Netanyahu told Fox News. Asked whether there was any indication as of now of Iran's involvement, he replied: "It's too early to say". Preliminary findings from a separate Israeli investigation, suggest that the alleged attacker intended to crash the plane, an Israeli security source told BBC Arabic. Eyewitness accounts and a statement by Netanyahu confirmed one of the pilots had stabbed the other and, according to the Israeli prime minister, "apparently tried to crash" the aircraft. One passenger, Hayun, described how he and others on the flight had restrained the attacker. He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane and after it levelled out, another pilot took over control. Flydubai said "an altercation occurred in the flight deck" and the flight was "successfully secured by on-duty Flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk airport". All of the airline's flights to and from Israel will be suspended during the investigation, a spokesperson said in a statement.
